panels.figure_caption: Ultrasonography of left breast showing a cystic lesion.
in_text_mentions: On physical examination, a soft and spongy mass was palpable in the left breast (Fig. 1). A breast ultrasound was performed, revealing an oblong, well-defined cystic mass with regular contours, an anechoic content containing fine mobile echogenic echoes, and a few thin, incomplete septa, measuring 37 × 46 mm (Fig. 2). The ultrasound concluded to a cystic breast mass, most likely a galactocele. A hormonal workup including prolactin, luteinising hormone, follicle-stimulating hormone, and estradiol was performed, with all values within the normal range.

The overlying nipple and skin were normal, and no nipple discharge was yielded upon gentle pressure. The right breast was normal. Examination of external genitalia revealed a normal male appearance with 4 cm penile length. Bilateral testes were descended with normal size, 1-2 mL in volume. s followed up for one year with no sign of spontaneous regression and thus surgery was performed at 3 years old. The mass was excised in total with a semicircular infra-areolar incision uneventfully (Figure 1). Histopathological examination of the excised specimen revealed an irregularly shaped cystic tissue containing dilated ducts, which were lined by cuboidal epithelium with proteinaceous secretory material in the luminal space (Figure 4). panels.rationale: Single-panel ultrasound of a left axillary accessory breast mass in an article specifically titled as galactocele. The panel is a real patient ultrasound and the disease attribution is supported by the disease-focused article title plus the captioned axillary mass. The available vocabulary finding for hypoechoic galactocele breast mass is applied to the hypoechoic mass; the solid-like irregular margins and nonparallel orientation are proposed because they are not in the vocabulary. Atypical because the lesion mimicked a suspicious malignant solid mass on ultrasound.
panels.attribution_text: Farrokh et al. Galactocele in the Axillary Accessory Breast Mimicking Suspicious Solid Mass on Ultrasound.. Case reports in obstetrics and gynecology 2017. doi:10.1155/2017/4807013. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Ultrasound examination of the axillary mass reveals a hypoechoic mass with irregular margins.
in_text_mentions: Physical examination revealed a 4 cm mass in the subcutaneous tissue of the left axilla. The mass was nontender and unattached to skin. There were no evidences of inflammation such as skin color discoloration in the left axilla or fever. Ultrasound examination of the axillary region revealed a hypoechoic, well-defined mass with irregular shape and margins and nonparallel orientation measuring 2.5∗3.5∗4 cm which was suspicious for a malignant lesion (Figure 1).
